question: How Do I Add a Custom Fee at Checkout, Like a Handling Charge?
metaDescription: WooCommerce's fees API supports this directly through a simple hook — no separate plugin needed for a straightforward flat or percentage-based fee.
shortAnswer: WooCommerce has a built-in fees API specifically for this, accessible through the woocommerce_cart_calculate_fees hook — a small snippet can add a flat amount, a percentage of the cart total, or a conditional fee (only above/below a certain order value, for instance) without needing a separate plugin for straightforward cases.

image.alt: A custom handling fee added to the checkout total through WooCommerce's built-in fees hook, alongside shipping and tax

bodyHtml:
How to Add a Fee

The woocommerce_cart_calculate_fees action runs during cart/checkout total calculation, and calling WC()->cart->add_fee() within it adds a named fee line to the order total, displayed clearly alongside the subtotal, shipping, and tax.

add_action( 'woocommerce_cart_calculate_fees', function( $cart ) {
    if ( is_admin() && ! defined( 'DOING_AJAX' ) ) {
        return;
    }
    $cart->add_fee( __( 'Handling Fee', 'textdomain' ), 4.99 );
} );

Things Worth Getting Right

  • The admin/AJAX check shown above is important — without it, the fee can be added incorrectly in admin-side calculations, causing confusing discrepancies.
  • Percentage-based fees are calculated the same way, just computing the amount from $cart->get_subtotal() or the full cart total rather than using a fixed number.
  • Conditional fees (only for orders below a minimum, or only for a specific payment method) need additional logic within the same hook to check the relevant condition before calling add_fee().
  • Tax handling on the fee itself needs deciding — add_fee() accepts a taxable parameter, and getting this wrong can cause the fee to be taxed (or not) incorrectly relative to the store's actual tax obligations.
  • Displaying the reason for the fee clearly to customers (a well-chosen fee name, or accompanying text) avoids confusion and support questions about an unexpected line item.

Implementing It Properly

  1. Use the woocommerce_cart_calculate_fees hook with the admin/AJAX guard included.
  2. Decide the fee's tax treatment correctly for the store's specific tax obligations.
  3. Test with different cart combinations, including any conditional logic, to confirm the fee applies exactly when intended.
